title: Spain Stunned! Tiny Cape Verde Holds Soccer Giants to a 0-0 Tie
summary: What if your country's whole population could fit inside a big city—and you still tied one of the best soccer teams on Earth? That's what Cape Verde did on Monday! This tiny African island nation, with only about 500,000 people, played its first World Cup game ever against Spain. And guess what? They didn't lose! The game ended 0-0. Spain is a soccer superpower. They won the World Cup in 2010 and have some of the world's best players. But they couldn't find a way past Cape Verde's goalkeeper, Vozinha. He was like a wall! He stopped shot after shot, even clawing away a header right before halftime. Spain's biggest star, 18-year-old Lamine Yamal, didn't start the game because he's still getting better after a leg injury. When he finally came in during the second half, the crowd went wild. He made some great passes and almost set up a goal, but Cape Verde held strong. In the very last minute, Cape Verde almost scored and won the game! A player named Diney Borges headed the ball toward the goal, but Spain's goalie caught it. That would have been the biggest shock in World Cup history. Spain's coach said his team is the best in the tournament, but they sure didn't look like it. They had the ball most of the time but moved too slowly. Even the fans booed when the referee stopped the game for a water break because it wasn't even hot inside the air-conditioned stadium! Cape Verde's players celebrated like they'd won. For a country making its debut on the world's biggest stage, a tie against Spain feels like a victory. Spain has to play better next time against Saudi Arabia, or they might be in big trouble.
why_it_matters: This story shows that hard work, teamwork, and staying calm can help an underdog stand up to a giant—a lesson that applies in sports, school, and life.

keywords.explanation: A superpower in sports means a country that is extremely strong and usually wins.
A debut is the first time a person or team appears in a competition.
The goalkeeper is the player who stays near the goal and tries to stop the ball from going in.
Clawing away means reaching out quickly with your hands to push something away, like a goalie saving a shot.
Air-conditioned means a building has machines that keep the air cool.
A shock is a big, unexpected surprise that nobody saw coming.

background_read: Cape Verde (pronounced 'kape-VER-day') is a small group of islands off the coast of Africa with only about 500,000 people. Spain is a soccer superpower that won the World Cup in 2010. Lamine Yamal (an 18-year-old wonderkid who plays for Barcelona) is one of the most exciting young players in the world.
Article_Structure: WHO: Cape Verde and Spain national soccer teams, especially goalkeeper Vozinha and young star Lamine Yamal.
WHAT: Cape Verde held Spain to a 0-0 tie in their first World Cup match, a huge surprise.
WHERE: At an air-conditioned World Cup stadium.
WHY: Spain moved the ball too slowly and couldn't get past Cape Verde's determined goalkeeper, while Cape Verde almost scored a last‑second winning goal.

perspectives.description: For Cape Verde, a 0-0 draw against a world champion feels like winning a trophy, and the whole country celebrated a historic debut.
Spain fans were frustrated because their team had so much possession but could not turn it into goals, and now face pressure in the next game.
Experts know that in a tournament, one surprising draw doesn’t ruin a team, but it does show that no opponent should be taken lightly, no matter how small the nation.
